key_insight: MedJev delivers competitive zero-shot medical predictions in a single forward pass on a laptop, but patient-level confidence estimates need local recalibration.
clinical_relevance: Low computational demands could support locally run clinical decision-support research, though predictive performance alone does not establish clinical safety or benefit.
method: Evaluated an open System One model across 10 medical benchmarks.
Compared zero-shot predictions with LLM baselines, published GPT results, and supervised models.
Tested two-parameter local recalibration using 50–200 labeled examples.
evidence_signal: On MIMIC-IV patient-level tasks, mortality AUROC was 0.926 versus XGBoost’s 0.902, while ED admission AUROC was lower than a supervised comparator (0.745 versus 0.809); recalibration reduced reported ECE from 0.286 to 0.007.
watch_item: Strong discrimination did not ensure reliable confidence estimates, and performance varied by task; local validation and calibration remain important before clinical use.
paper_title: MedJev: Evaluating Zero-Shot System-One Decision Making in Medicine
